reviews.suggested_text: But you were holy, spiritual beings, living an eternal life; yet you defiled yourselves in the blood of women[a], begot children through the blood of flesh, lusted in human blood[b], and made flesh and blood as they do—those who die and perish[c].
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace all existing notes. [a] after 'women': 'The first blood-expression is daggered in the selected edition. Charles, p42 n10, identifies corruption and proposes በደመ, supported by Greek ἐν τῷ αἵματι. “In the blood of women” translates that explicit repair, not an uncontested source reading.' This rendering takes it with making or producing; the following mortality clause concerns mortal flesh-and-blood beings. “Perish” may also be rendered “be destroyed.”' Delete the previous-rendering note, which does not explain either crux.
